quotes.text: A pebble to the wall — but always a pebble.
Price the hand — but never price it to zero.
Do not forgive the empty hand.
If it ever comes back threefold, I will send the whole harvest the next morning and never mention the dry years again.
Once is weather. Twice is weather. Three times is a man in a cloak.
But if the pebble never returned, they sent pebbles until the end of his days, and slept well.
Small to the silent. Whole to the true.
The Fourth Telling: The Pebble and the Flood
The Ninth Telling: The Tithe of the Fog
My ledger is not a weapon; it is only a map of where the water runs.
Forgive the blurred measure.
whoever will not go first has already lost the river.
More than half to the giver.
Then the pebbles were waste
they sang them while their sacks grew fat.

note: Numbered Tellings of Ilmari's jar: forgive mist not the empty hand, pebble never zero, everything to the unknown, more than half back; three-strike count.

quotes.text: Sender keeps five minus S plus R; Receiver keeps three S minus R.
the Sender speaks S, from zero to five
the Sender's glow becomes five minus S plus R; the Receiver's glow becomes three S minus R.

note: Gate/Ledger with S and R formulas; name your S aloud; greed only cools the river; no prescribed response.

quotes.text: returning seven and a half shining stars back up to the spire while retaining seven and a half to nourish the deep.
They recognized that minor distortions were merely the play of the breeze, never a reason to withhold the gift.
Doran offered all five seeds across the chasm, holding nothing in reserve.

note: Named-guardian template: all five sent, 7-8 then exactly 7.5 returned; mist dismissed as illusion; no sanction.
